passages.happening:
The heading reads, “For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David, the servant of the LORD” (verse 1). The psalm begins with a look inside a wicked man: “There is no fear of God before his eyes” (verse 1). “For his eyes are too full of conceit to detect or hate his own sin” (verse 2). “Even on his bed he plots wickedness” (verse 4).

Then, suddenly, the psalm looks up. “Your loving devotion, O LORD, reaches to the heavens, Your faithfulness to the clouds” (verse 5). “Your righteousness is like the highest mountains; Your judgments are like the deepest sea” (verse 6).

People find shelter and a feast with God: “How precious is Your loving devotion, O God, that the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings!” (verse 7). “For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light” (verse 9).

It ends with a prayer for protection, and a picture of evil fallen: “There the evildoers lie fallen, thrown down and unable to rise” (verse 12).
passages.hearers:
The heading calls David ‘the servant of the LORD’, as Psalm 18 does. It is an honour title, given to people God chose for a task, such as Moses.

Verse 1 uses a word normally used for a prophet's message, ‘an oracle’. The Hebrew of this verse is hard, and Bibles translate it differently. The point is clear enough: sin speaks to the wicked man from inside, and he listens.

Then the psalm uses the biggest things in the world to measure God's love: the sky, the clouds, the highest mountains, the deepest sea. The wicked man lies on his bed making small plans. God's love is larger than the world.

A fountain was a spring of fresh water, life itself in a dry land. The ‘river of delights’ (verse 8) may recall Eden, the garden watered by a river.
passages.later:
Paul quotes verse 1 at the end of his list of human sins: “There is no fear of God before their eyes” (Romans 3:18).

Jesus offered the fountain of verse 9: “whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst” (John 4:14). John's Gospel calls him the light of the world, and Revelation ends with “a river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb” (Revelation 22:1).
passages.asks:
The psalm asks what you are looking at. The wicked man looks at his own schemes until he cannot see his sin. The psalmist looks up at God and sees everything more clearly. ‘In Your light we see light.’

Verse 2 is also a warning. Ask God to show you the sins you have stopped noticing.
